summary.headline: Aurobindo Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to Rs 9,150 crore; operating EBITDA Rs 1,924 crore (21% margin) after a Rs 43 crore one-time charge; FY27 guidance reiterated.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16% YoY to Rs 9,150 crore, with formulations at Rs 8,101 crore (89% of sales) growing 17%. Operating EBITDA was Rs 1,924 crore at a 21% margin, after a Rs 43 crore one-time loss on derecognition of leased residuals, and PAT was Rs 1,032 crore. The Lannett acquisition closed after FTC approval, and management reiterated FY27 guidance of double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin above 21% and absolute EBITDA above Rs 8,000 crore. Management was largely forthcoming on biosimilars, CDMO economics and Lannett, but declined to give specifics on Lannett's product pipeline and the Europe upfront payment.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 8,101 crore, up 17% YoY, about 89% of consolidated revenue, with growth across all key markets.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,049 crore, about 11% of revenue, supported by backward integration; PEN-G producing 800-900 tonnes per month, with 6-APA and Amoxicillin output improving.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 3,770 crore ($399 million), up 8.1% YoY; 10 new products launched, 9 ANDAs filed and 10 final approvals received in the quarter.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR 267 million, up 11% YoY in constant currency; Europe EBITDA margin reached about 20%, and management guides double-digit growth for FY27.

segments.name: Growth markets
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,063 crore ($113 million), up 38% YoY, with growth spread across countries rather than one outlier market.

segments.name: ARV formulations
segments.commentary: Stable at $35 million for the quarter on stable volumes.

segments.name: Eugia (injectables)
segments.commentary: Management guides single-digit growth for FY27 (not double-digit) with about Rs 500 crore-plus revenue, due to lack of new approvals, mainly at unit 3 under remediation.

segments.name: China OSD facility
segments.commentary: Output doubled over the past 12 months; capacity is above 2 billion tablets against about 500 million-plus last year; FY26 EBITDA was a loss of about $7 million, and management expects a positive EBITDA this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reiterated: double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin north of 21%, absolute EBITDA above Rs 8,000 crore, with potential upside from high-value businesses.
Tax rate expected to normalise to 28-29% by year-end from 31.9% in Q1.
R&D for FY27 expected at about Rs 1,450-1,500 crore, the maximum per CFO, as most biosimilar Phase 3 studies are complete.
Europe: management expects FY27 to close with double-digit growth and further EBITDA expansion.
Eugia: single-digit growth in FY27 with about Rs 500 crore-plus revenue.
Asked about a run rate of Rs 2,200 crore per quarter from next quarter, the CFO said it is the target, subject to the Middle East geopolitical situation.
TheraNym unit 1 steady revenue from 2028 (stockpiling dependent); unit 2 commissioning by end 2029 and revenue from 2031; CMO revenue of $150-200 million by 2032 at 35-50% EBITDA margin.
Biosimilars: 7-8 products in EU, UK and Canada by 2028-29 (four approved); at least three US filings in 2026, with the first US filing imminent.
Lannett: 12-month plan to bring in site transfers and raise utilisation from about 40%; management expects Lannett's net sales of at least $60 million per quarter without new launches.
capex_capacity: Net capex of $78 million in Q1, mainly for TheraNym Biologics.
TheraNym unit 1 inaugurated on 3 June 2026; qualification of facility and equipment to begin by November 2026; validation batches in 2027.
TheraNym unit 2 (pure-play drug substance) construction to begin October 2026 subject to clearances; commissioning targeted by end 2029.
Lannett: about 40% utilisation with large unutilised capacity; can manufacture up to about 350 million units with limited capex, plus the Aurolife unit and one reserve facility.
PEN-G: production of 800-900 tonnes per month, with capacity cited at 15,000 tonnes per annum; India demand 9,000-10,000 tonnes.
China OSD: capacity above 2 billion tablets; objective to go beyond 2 billion by end of this year or mid next year.
demand_pricing: Growth markets: Indonesia, China and Canada newly contributing; no single country drove the growth.

Europe: most oncology biosimilars are sold via tenders with a 2-3 quarter lag before supply; Denosumab and Omalizumab are retail products. Three commercial routes in Europe: own Aurobindo Europe, Orion (Nordics and Baltics) and STADA (duplicate MA for an oncology product expected soon).
Europe antibiotics: the peak season is Sep-Oct, so higher antibiotic sales are expected in the coming months.

Lannett: controlled substance quotas are capped nationally and allocated across suppliers, so no sudden jump is expected; growth is expected from new launches including Advair (launch in August 2026).
PEN-G: Indian imports of 6-APA have fallen sharply; MIP expected to be reached by year-end; PLI payment expected in September or March.
CRO: A1 Biochem has about Rs 100 crore turnover, 50+ customers and 800+ projects; closing expected in 1-2 months; management plans to build an integrated CRDMO.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Advair launch delayed and what is the Lannett pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Swami Iyer said the launch is not delayed; Advair launches in August 2026, with inventory build-up needed before launch. Other products are confidential.

qa_highlights.question: How will Lannett's underutilised plant be used, and when does Lannett reach Aurobindo's US margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 40%. A 12-month plan transfers unlaunched or underperforming site products and government-business products. Management expects utilisation gains within months and benefits over about nine months, and declined to give a margin timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing of TheraNym revenues and the unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 1 revenue is steady from 2028 after customer stockpiling; unit 2 revenue from 2031. CMO revenue of $150-200 million by 2032 at 35-50% EBITDA margin, depending on product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an upfront payment from STADA, and how is it accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: No upfront has been received; STADA covers regulatory filing costs for the duplicate MA, and accounting will be reviewed with auditors once received.

qa_highlights.question: Why is R&D lower this quarter, and what is the FY27 R&D guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 3 studies for most wave-one biosimilars are complete, with one finishing next year. Q1 R&D was about Rs 344 crore versus Rs 367 crore a year earlier; FY27 is expected at about Rs 1,450-1,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How does Aurobindo respond to US onshoring requirements?
qa_highlights.answer: Lannett (up to about 350 million units with limited capex) plus Aurolife can meet significant US demand, with a reserve facility available. Management argued any mandate would need to be level-playing, otherwise imports would be displaced.

risks_watch: Eugia unit 3 remediation and lack of new approvals constrain growth to single digits.
Lannett: controlled substance quotas are capped and Advair launch and integration timing need tracking; the Rs 43 crore one-time charge shows some asset-related cost.
PEN-G/6-APA: pricing risk from cheaper imports if MIP and PLI support is not secured; PLI payment timing is uncertain.
US onshoring policy: possible manufacturing mandate and its cost impact.
TheraNym: revenue depends on customer stockpiling, and the unit 2 product mix is undecided.
Middle East geopolitical situation may affect the Rs 2,200 crore quarterly run-rate target.
Biosimilar US filings (first filing imminent) and EU tender-based timing; no Europe upfront disclosed.
key_quotes: We continue to reiterate our FY27 guidance to double -digit revenue growth, with EBITDA margins north of 21% and absolute EBITDA in excess of 8000, with potential upside driven by positive outperformance in our high-value strategic business areas.
This year has been a steady growth, but it is not going to be double digit. It will be single digit because of lack of new approvals, both from unit, mainly from unit three.
We should be looking at it. But let us wait how the geopolitical situation in the Middle East is getting over.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the base business, Lannett integration, biosimilar timelines and Europe, with the CFO reiterating FY27 guidance. Cautious and deliberately vague on Lannett's pipeline, Eugia growth (cut to single digits), the Rs 2,200 crore run-rate (tied to the Middle East situation) and the STADA upfront, which management would not quantify.

TheraNym Biologics unit 2 pure-play drug substance; construction from Oct 2026, commissioning end 2029, revenue from 2031
China OSD facility capacity above 2 billion tablets (output doubled over 12 months), target beyond 2 billion by end of year or mid next year

growth.why: FY27 double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin >21% and absolute EBITDA >Rs 8,000 cr reiterated; backing is partial: Lannett at ~40% utilisation with up to ~350m units, Europe/growth markets momentum, and China OSD capacity, but Eugia cut to single-digit and TheraNym capacity only lands 2028-2031.
